perspective:
Vincent Chinana’s available information/experience:

- He knows his own identity/background: Alaska Native man, mechanic, middle-school education; he tends to be practical, cautious, and detail-oriented.
- He knows Patrick Guzman as a long-time friend since their teenage years, a Latino construction worker, with whom he shares a blue-collar bond and often collaborates—Vincent’s mechanical skills plus Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At the diner, Vincent learned Patrick was considering a new construction venture to expand his business. Vincent had heard it was risky. He told Patrick he was worried about financial security and suggested Patrick reconsider or delay until gathering more information. Patrick said it seemed like a good opportunity, thought it was worth the risk, was still weighing options, appreciated Vincent’s concern, and would think it over.
- Days later, Vincent noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent told Patrick he felt Patrick was not telling him everything and that he felt betrayed as a friend. Patrick said it was complicated, he hadn’t wanted to worry Vincent with details, apologized for not being transparent, and offered to sit down and explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, Vincent learned the investment troubles were serious. Patrick said it had been tough and he might lose a significant amount if it didn’t turn around soon. Vincent offered to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses; Patrick thanked him and expressed gratitude.
- A month later, at a coffee shop, Vincent knew/believed the venture might actually turn a profit. Patrick said it was starting to look up and he was relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologized for doubting him and proposed a joint venture. Patrick agreed and said they should work out details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick were optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent said their combined skills could make it succeed. Patrick was excited. They agreed to start drafting a business plan, outline every step carefully, cover all bases, and set it up for success.
- Vincent’s own actions include: questioning Patrick’s plan, expressing worry, confronting Patrick about transparency, offering a loan, apologizing for doubting him, proposing the joint venture, and initiating business-plan drafting.
- Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s unspoken thoughts, undisclosed financial details, or any events between meetings that Vincent did not observe or hear about.
